title: candidate-feedback-draft-amelia-reyes-serving-runtime-engineer
content:
Quick notes / draft feedback for Amelia Reyes — applied for Serving Runtime Engineer (L4)

Summary:
- Strong infra background: 4 years building model-serving features at previous company (EdgeScale). Good at system-level reasoning (routing, batching, cache).
- Comfortable in Python + C++ combo; has tinkered with CUDA kernels but limited heavy kernel dev. Familiar with quantization concepts (QAT/INT8) and had an ownership story for a quantized runtime integration.
- Great communicator, clear about trade-offs and constraints. Very pragmatic.
- Weakness: limited production-scale multi-tenant experience (did single-tenant deployments mostly), and relatively light experience with large-model KV cache internals.

Interview breakdown (notes to self):
1) Phone screen (30m) — Lena
- Good high-level: explained batching strategies, difference between synchronous vs async inference, when to prioritize latency vs throughput. Emphasized isolating tail-latency via preemptible pooling.
- Asked about monitoring: uses Prometheus + custom p99 instrumentation.
- Red flag? none. Comfortable with fundamental infra concepts.

2) Take-home / system design (1h) — Panel: Jordan + Priya
- Given design prompt: "Design a multi-model inference service with prefix caching and dynamic batching."
- Amelia laid out core components: router, worker pool, KV cache sharding (LRU-eviction), batching service with adaptive batch sizing based on latency SLOs.
- Nice details: suggested using async RPC for router->worker to avoid head-of-line blocking, and using request coalescing for identical prefixes (cache hit aggregation).
- Missing detail: how to migrate cache shards safely during autoscale (we discussed consistent hashing vs lease-based ownership; she hadn't implemented shard migration before but understood the trade-offs).

3) Coding (45m) — live pair (Priya)
- Implemented a simplified streaming token emission simulator in Python. Code correct, clean, used generators to model streaming early flush.
- Edge-case handling: handled cancellation and backpressure, but initial implementation had an off-by-one bug in buffer flush which she quickly fixed after test failure.
- Time management: good.

4) Deep dive (30m) — architecture + past project (Jordan)
- Walked through her work on a quantized inference pipeline: how they validated accuracy drop, ran A/B on small prompts, and added a fallback to fp16 for long-tail prompts. Good product-minded thinking.
- On CUDA/kernels: she wrote some CUDA prototypes but handed off production kernels to an internal team. So not strong as a kernel author, but able to work with kernel teams.

Scorecard (L1-L5 scale):
- System design / architecture: 4
- Coding: 4
- Production ops / SRE thinking: 3
- Low-level performance (CUDA/kernels): 3
- Communication / cross-team: 5
- Product sense (trade-offs, evals): 4

Overall recommendation (draft): Strong hire for L4 depending on scope. I recommend moving forward with an on-site (or final panel) focused on production-scale multi-tenant scenarios and a short kernel-contrib take-home or pairing session if we care about low-level kernel work.

Suggested hire band / IC level: L4. If we need kernel authorship (L5), note that Amelia would need a ramp and pairing with our kernel team; she could still be productive owning router/batching/cache and orchestration layers.

Open questions / follow-ups before final offer:
- Ask for a concrete example where she instrumented and diagnosed a tail-latency issue in production (details: tools, metrics, mitigation).
- Clarify extent of multi-tenant load testing and autoscale experience (did she operate 100s of tenants, or single large tenant?).
- Verify familiarity with consistent-hashing and live shard migration — she knows the theory but less hands-on.
- If kernel expertise matters, propose a short (2-3 hour) pairing session with our kernel engineer to evaluate low-level comfort.

Suggested next interviewers / panel:
- SRE lead (latency/observability): Priya Desai
- Kernel / performance engineer: Alex Kim or Samir Patel
- Senior runtime engineer (batching/caching): Jordan Rivera

Administrative notes:
- Candidate timezone: PST — flexible.
- Compensation expectation: mid-range for L4 (candidate mentioned current comp but not exact).
- References: requested 2, candidate said can provide within 48 hours.

Decision options: Proceed to final panel + reference check (preferred) / Hold for kernel pairing (if kernel skill is blocking).

Notes to self: polish this into the standard scorecard template on Confluence (link above) and sync with Priya + Jordan before sending formal feedback.

--- END ---
